references.text: The same principle that the thank offering must be eaten on the same day it is sacrificed, without leaving anything until morning.
The Passover lamb was also not to be left until morning but burned up—the same principle of not letting sacrificial meat remain until the next day.
Consecration offerings that were not eaten on the same day were to be burned with fire and not eaten—a parallel rule regarding sacrificial leftovers.
Repetition of the rule that peace offerings must be eaten on the day of sacrifice or the following day, with the remainder burned.
Continuation of the same law text elaborating on the rules for vow offerings and voluntary offerings.
Refers to the peace offering (שְׁלָמִים) mentioned in connection with the thank offering in the main verse.
